_comment: THE RECIPE BOOK (docs/plan_crafting_and_materials.md section 3). ONE STRUCTURE: inputs -> outputs, both lists of THINGS, where a thing is a material or a piece of equipment. An alloy, a sled and a loom are the same record with different rows - bronze is not a special case and neither is a tool. A RECIPE READS ONE CHARACTERISTIC (`reads`), and that is what makes 'there is no best hide' real: the sled reads toughness and the hurdles read suppleness, so a mammoth pelt makes an excellent sled and poor lashings and a hare pelt does the reverse. Spending the wrong hide on the wrong thing is a mistake the player is free to make. PLAYTEST DIALS.
_comment_work_and_costs: `work` IS WORKER-TURNS FOR ONE OUTPUT PASS, at progress_per_worker_turn x a rate of 1.0. The bench accrues workers x progress_per_worker_turn x craft_speed, and craft_speed is the bounding tool's equipped value or - with no tool - the MATERIAL's own hand_working.rate, which is 0.5 on all three organics and would be 0 for something that cannot be worked bare-handed at all. THAT ZERO IS THE WHOLE REFUSAL MECHANISM: there is no 'you cannot craft that' branch anywhere in the sim, exactly as max(0, attack - defense) refuses a hunt. THE COSTS ARE SIZED SO MATERIAL, NOT BENCH TIME, IS WHAT BINDS. THE CROOK IS PRICED AS THE `hoes` ARE - bone + fibre at `work: 5` - because it is the same class of tool on the other web; the two build kits must not diverge on price for a reason nobody chose. THE HURDLES RECIPE IS THE ONE OUTPUT THAT IS NOT KIT: it makes a MATERIAL the `animal:pen` rung eats (4 wood + 2 hide -> 1 hurdle, `work: 7`), so its cost is judged against that rung's own pile of 6 rather than against the kit clock - a pen is 24 wood, 12 hide and 42 bench-turns, and the wood is what the spawn's `start_stock` supplies until forest foraging lands. Against the shipped ~17-worker band (equipment.md's kit clock): a gathering half of ~8.5 reaches ~68 biomass a turn, so reeds at 0.02 fibre/biomass pay ~1.4 fibre a turn; a hunting half on Red Deer hauls ~45 biomass, paying ~0.6 hide, ~0.09 bone and ~0.04 fibre. So 6 hide is ~10 turns of banked hide and 5 fibre is ~4 turns of banked fibre, while a 4-hand bench works a `work: 8` sled off in 4 turns bare-handed. BONE IS THE SCARCE ONE BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE (0.0012-0.003 per biomass against hide's 0.006-0.022), so nothing costs more than 3 of it, and that scarcity is what makes Bone-working the slow craft with no dial saying so. AGAINST THE ~15-20 TURN KIT CLOCK (the whole band on that one job, not the half that banks the material): baskets run dry in ~18.5 turns and cost ~4 turns of fibre plus ~2 of hide to replace, so a band keeps its kit alive on roughly a quarter of its material income and spends the rest on tools and stock. Spears last ~42 turns and cost 1 bone, which is ~11 turns of hunting - comfortable. HOES ARE IN-FAMILY RATHER THAN DERIVED: a bone blade hafted with fibre is the same shape as spears and clubs, and `work: 5` sits between clubs (4) and spears (6) - the first build tool the plant web has ever had, so there is no predecessor number to invert. It ships UNGRADED, deliberately, so plant and animal build gear stay consistent until both gain grades together (issue #561). TOOLS ARE THE INVESTMENT: a tanning frame is 8 fibre + 2 bone, ~28 turns of banked material, and it then pays for itself over the 25 items it lasts.
_comment_knowledge: KNOWLEDGE GATES A RECIPE ONLY WHEN THE RECIPE SAYS SO. `requires_knowledge` is absent on every ordinary kit recipe - you can make a sled by hand on turn one, and DOING IT is what teaches Tanning. Every TOOL recipe carries one entry per material it is made from, and validate enforces exactly that: a named craft must be the craft of one of this recipe's own INPUT materials. Paired with the rule that a tool is never made from the material it bounds, that makes the deadlock UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely avoided - metal needing a crucible that needs metalworking cannot be written down here. TOOLS ARE EARNED, NEVER A PREREQUISITE: there is no opening move where everyone builds tools first, and a tool run dry drops the band back to the rate the game already ships at rather than into a spiral. THE LESSON IS THE RECIPE'S OWN `craft`, charged per ITEM COMPLETED on the same quantum as the tool's wear (intensification_ladder.json's `knowledge.craft_lesson_per_item`, in PRACTICE UNITS, against that craft's own `knowledge.lesson_costs` entry - the same currency and the same divisor a rung's lesson goes through, one quantum over), so what is being made decides what is learned.
_comment_grades: ONE QUALITY LADDER FOR THE WHOLE GAME - THE GRADES ARE THE BANDS. A grade is named by a `characteristic_bands` rung and a recipe declares NO seams of its own: the output's grade is the band of min(material reading, tool quality ceiling), resolved through the same table that rates the hide it was made from. The same four words rate the hide on the panel's rail and the sled you make out of it, so a reading of .55 is `good` in both places. An earlier cut invented coarse/standard/fine, which was a SECOND VOCABULARY FOR ONE IDEA - the player learned quality twice - and, worse, a second set of cut points free to drift from the bands beside them. CONTINUOUS IN, DISCRETE OUT: the reading never scales a resolved stat, it SELECTS a band, and the band declares ABSOLUTES (EquipmentEffect names the value a stat TAKES and has no representation for a multiplier stacking on something else, which is what keeps 'flat until expiry, then a step down' structural rather than remembered). A BAND A RECIPE DOES NOT DECLARE INHERITS THE ONE BELOW IT, so a recipe wanting three steps writes three - and validate rejects a grade key that is not a band, and a lowest grade that is not the FIRST band, because nothing would then answer for a reading of 0.0. THE ANCHOR IS DERIVED, NOT NAMED: it is the band the bench material's bare-handed hand_working.quality_ceiling falls in (0.60 on all three organics, which is `good`), and the grade resolved there must equal the output item's default tier - so a BARE-HANDED CRAFT OFF THE BEST MATERIAL A BAND CAN WORK BY HAND REPRODUCES THE SHIPPED ITEM EXACTLY, and a tool run dry drops the band back to the rate the game already ships at rather than into a spiral. The four rungs fan around that anchor at poor x0.75 / fair x0.85 / good x1.00 / excellent x1.15 - the design's own sled example, 30/34/40/46 on a shipped 40. A GRADE MAY ONLY DECLARE A STAT THE OUTPUT ITEM'S TIERS DECLARE, and must restate that effect's mass bounds verbatim: a grade REPLACES a number rather than adding one, and an excellent snare that dropped `max_body_mass` would quietly become a mammoth trap. A recipe with NO `grades` block says its payload is not tier-bought at all (the hoes' and the crook's `build_work`, the wayfinding gear's vantage, a bench tool's craft stats) - the batch is still STAMPED with the band it was made at, that band simply buys it no stat.
_comment_craft_is_derived: `craft` IS THE CRAFT OF THE MATERIAL THE RECIPE READS, and validate rejects any other value. It is written out because that is where a reader needs it, not because it is a second decision - one home per fact, guarded. That is also what keeps the whole model free of a 'primary material' field: the material the recipe READS is the material the bench works, whose tool is consulted, whose bare-handed rate applies and whose craft is practised.
_comment_hurdles: HURDLES ARE A MATERIAL NOW, NOT A PIECE OF EQUIPMENT (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.7): a fence panel goes into the ground and stays there, so it is spent by the `animal:pen` rung's build pile and its upkeep rate rather than carried to the next job. That is why this is the one shipped recipe whose output is a `material` rather than an `equipment` row - and why it declares no `grades`, exactly as it did as a kit item: a material-only output may not be graded, and a quality axis on a hurdle would invite 'a better fence contains better', the containment-scaling this slice defers. IT IS WOVEN WITHIES LASHED WITH HIDE THONG, so it costs 4 wood and 2 hide. THE HIDE IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE SIMPLIFIED OUT: this is the ONLY recipe in the book that reads `suppleness`, and _comment_reads_pairs' whole pillar is that each material's two axes are split between two recipes wanting opposite ends. A wood-only hurdle orphans that axis and makes the Thunder Mammoth strictly the best hide, deleting a decision the crafting arc built on purpose. AND THE CRAFT FOLLOWS THE `reads`, NOT THE OTHER WAY ROUND: `craft` is DERIVED (see _comment_craft_is_derived) - it is the craft of the material the recipe reads, validated - so reading hide's `suppleness` makes this a `tanning` bench, unchanged from when hurdles were kit. Wood's own `pliancy` is read a recipe away, by the stone-dressing tool whose haft has to give rather than shatter (see _comment_road_tools), so this recipe reading hide instead orphans nothing. THE PAIR WITH NO READER IS HURDLES' OWN (`stoutness` / `span`), and that one is deliberate.
_comment_crook: THE KIT ITEM HURDLES USED TO BE, minus the butchering quantum and the pen collection rate (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.9 item 12). Removing hurdles-as-equipment emptied two kits, and the `hurdling` kit takes this instead - one animal kit serving both husbandry keeping and animal builds, the shape `tillage` already has for plants; without it every tame, pen build and turn of herd keeping drops to bare-handed speed. Bone + fibre on `hoes`' own shape, and `reads: length` because a crook is a long staff - it joins `wayfinding` as a second reader of that axis, which breaks nothing since bone's pair already has a reader on each end. `work: 5.0` sits beside the hoes' own, deliberately: the two are the same class of tool on the two webs.
_comment_road_tools: THE TWO ROAD TOOLS ARE WOOD'S PAIR'S FIRST READERS, AND THEY WANT OPPOSITE ENDS OF IT. `hardness` / `pliancy` had no reader at all until now (see _comment_reads_pairs), which is why these two recipes are where the split lands rather than a third copy of bone's. EARTHMOVING READS `hardness`: a mattock is levered against packed ground turn after turn, so the haft has to hold its shape and not spring. STONE-DRESSING READS `pliancy`: a dressing hammer swung against stone sends the whole blow back up the shaft, and a haft that gives is a haft that does not shatter. So a hard, brittle timber makes excellent spades and poor mauls and a supple one does the exact reverse - the same trade the sled and the hurdles make of hide, one material over, and the reason neither wood is the upgrade. THE BONE IS THE WORKING END - the shod edge and the wedges - AND IT CARRIES NO `reads`, because a recipe may read exactly ONE axis (one reading selects one grade, and validate refuses a second). The wood is what the two tools disagree about, so the wood is what they read; bone's own pair is already answered for by spears/clubs on `density` and the crook and the wayfinding gear on `length`. WOOD 3 TO BONE 2 because these are big tools - mostly shaft, with a working end - and `work` 8.0 puts them above the crook's and the hoes' 5.0 for the same reason. `craft` IS WOOD'S OWN (weaving), not bone's, and that is validate's rule rather than a choice: a recipe's craft must be the craft of the material it WORKS - the one carrying `reads` - which is exactly why the hurdles are `tanning` off a wood-and-hide weave. These are shaped timber with a knapped end set into it, so the shaping is the craft. PLAYTEST DIALS: what these cost is what decides whether a faction roads its first link at turn 40 or turn 100.
_comment_reads_pairs: THE AXIS PAIRS ARE THE POINT, NOT THE ROWS. Each material's two axes are split between two recipes that want opposite ends, so no source is the upgrade: HIDE - the sled reads `toughness` (a drag harness wants a hide that will not tear) and the hurdles read `suppleness` (the thong the withies are lashed with has to be bent and knotted tight, not merely strong), so a Thunder Mammoth (tough 0.92 / supple 0.10) makes an excellent sled and poor lashings and a Snow Hare (0.14 / 0.92) does the exact reverse. That pairing is the reason the hurdles recipe KEEPS its hide input now that it is a weave off wood: this is the book's only reader of `suppleness`, and dropping it would make the mammoth strictly the best hide. FIBRE - baskets read `fineness` (a close weave holds small loose things) and traps read `strength` (a snare is a cord that has to hold), so Cotton (fine 0.92 / strong 0.35) makes excellent baskets and fair snares while Mesquite bast (0.30 / 0.70) is the other way; Flax (0.88 / 0.80) is good at both, which is why it is worth sowing. BONE - spears and clubs read `density` (how well it holds a point, how hard it hits) and wayfinding gear and the crook read `length` (a tally stave and a shepherd's staff both need a long piece), so a Thunder Mammoth tusk (dense 0.88 / long 0.95) is excellent for either while a Rabbit Warren's (0.28 / 0.06) is barely a piece at all. WOOD - the two ROAD TOOLS are that pair's readers and they want opposite ends of it: earthmoving reads `hardness` (a mattock haft is levered against packed ground and must hold its shape) and stone-dressing reads `pliancy` (a maul haft takes the blow back up the shaft and must give rather than shatter), so a hard brittle timber makes excellent spades and poor mauls - see _comment_road_tools. HURDLES' own pair (`stoutness` / `span`) is the one with no reader: a material must be rated to exist, and nothing in the sim consults either of those - deliberately, since a quality axis on a fence panel invites 'a better fence contains better'.
_comment_tools: THE THREE BENCH TOOLS, AND THE TWO RULES THEY EXIST TO DEMONSTRATE. (1) A MATERIAL'S TOOL IS NEVER MADE FROM THAT MATERIAL: the tanning frame is fibre and bone, the loom is bone and hide, the bone awl is fibre and hide. Otherwise you would need the scarce material to make the thing that stretches it, which is the opposite of what a tool is for. (2) A TOOL IS GATED ON THE CRAFTS OF WHAT IT IS MADE FROM, NEVER ON THE CRAFT IT UNLOCKS - the tanning frame needs Weaving and Bone-working (its two materials) and pointedly NOT Tanning (the craft it serves). Otherwise metal needs a crucible, the crucible needs metalworking, and nothing can start. Both rules are enforced by validate, and together they make the deadlock unwriteable. THE LADDER THEN FALLS OUT WITH NOTHING ADDED: weave baskets bare-handed -> learn Weaving -> knap spears bare-handed -> learn Bone-working -> build a tanning frame -> hide work gets faster, cheaper and can reach `excellent` -> and the same shape repeats the day clay and metal have producers. WHAT EACH TOOL BUYS is on the item in equipment.json, beside its durability.
